name: FT Fuel Production - Nuclear with Steam Export
Polylactic acid (PLA) end-of-life
notes:
PLA is capable of biodegradation under certain conditions, It is assumed that the end-of-life of PLA is landfill and the degration will occurr at 48% ratio. Thus, the rest (52%) biogenic carbon in PLA is sequestered.
50% of biodegradable carbon is released as CH4, and the rest becomes CO2. Since CO2 is biogenic emission, only CH4 is accounted for GHG calculation.
CH4 capture is considered here using EPA WARM parameters, LFG collection rate of 75% and oxidation rate of 36%. Refer to Benavides, T.P. et al. Life cycle greenhouse gas emissions and energy use of polylactic acid,
bio-derived polyethylene, and fossil-derived polyethylene, Journal of Cleaner Production, 2020, 277, 124010.
